newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada mum on attending new Hong Kong legislature.
newsitem.headline: Canada mum on attending new Hong Kong legislature.

text.p: Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy declined on Friday to say whether he would attend the controversial swearing-in of the Beijing-picked legislature in Hong Kong on July 1.

An official news release on Friday said he would attend handover ceremonies that day, but departmental spokeswoman Jennifer Ledwidge said she still could not say whether a Canadian representative would attend the actual swearing-in.
"Mr. Axworthy is consulting with other nations and most recently the European Union," Ledwidge told Reuters, adding that she expected him to make an announcement in Hong Kong.
Britain and the United States this week reversed their pledge to boycott the investiture, agreeing to send diplomats.

When France and other nations decided in April to stop co-sponsoring an annual U.N. human rights resolution critical of China, Canada quickly announced it also would not join the resolution, citing the crumbling consensus.

Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien has generally pushed trade expansion during his 3-1/2 years in power, eschewing boycotts and other measures aimed at human rights abuses in favour of what he calls constructive engagement.
